A long-lived token (Anthropic’s official `claude setup-token`, the same one the Claude Code GitHub Action uses) lets this subscription run on remote machines and paired devices WITHOUT shipping its interactive login: it lasts 1 year and never rotates, so nothing can get out of sync. This is the intended way to run your own subscription on your own remote/CI machines — safer than shipping the login. It still bills YOUR subscription and is tied to it, so treat it like the account itself; Anthropic recommends an API key instead when a credential is shared broadly across many contexts. Limits: quota refresh (⟳) does not work through it, and when it expires sessions fail until you re-mint.

VibeSpace's own agent tools — its browser (vibespace-browser), status, task, inbox, messages, desktop windows, channels, manuals, and the list of its published pages — run without a permission card for every step, in every permission mode. Only these tools: any other command still asks, and so does the part of a command line that runs something else. Starting a background shell command (vibespace-job run) still asks, because it can run anything, and publishing a page (vibespace-page publish) asks every time, unless the session runs with full access (Never ask), where it runs as it always did. The trade-off: anything the agent can read, it can type or upload into a web page without asking — except an upload from ~/.claude, ~/.ssh, ~/.vibespace, ~/.codex or VibeSpace's account stores, which the browser tool refuses. The browser tool also writes files (a screenshot, a PDF, a download) only under the project directory, /tmp or ~/Downloads — never over your keys, logins or config. Off = every step asks again. Applies to newly started and resumed sessions; nothing is written to your Claude settings file.

What: data/usage-history/_held could not be listed ({code}) since {since} — VibeSpace cannot tell which months of which machine are held, so a month that needs its hold (out of shape, or still being recorded from it) is not recorded yet; its machine keeps those events and sends them again.

What: data/usage-history/_held/{file} could not be read ({code}) since {since} — the events of {month} held for {machine} stay on the disk, unread. Until it is read, the new events of {month} from that machine wait (it keeps them and sends them again) unless the month's file is in shape; its other months are recorded as usual.

What: data/usage-history/_held/{file} — the record of the held events of {month} that were dropped past the bound — could not be read ({code}). VibeSpace set it aside unread, bytes intact, as data/usage-history/_set-aside/{aside}; the count of dropped events it named is not known.
What: data/usage-history/{shard} is back in shape — the events of {month} held beside it while it was not are recorded into it first, in order.
What: data/usage-history/{shard} is {size} and holds about {ratio}× its distinct rows — the same events written again and again.
What: data/usage-history/{shard} is {size} and holds more distinct ids than its index may keep.
What: data/usage-history/{shard} is {size} — over the 2 GiB bound, and a dedup pass found no repeated row in it.
What: data/usage-history/{shard} is {size} — past the 2 GiB a month of usage never needs.

What: line {line} of data/usage-history/_held/{file} is no record VibeSpace writes. VibeSpace copied the file as it was, bytes intact, to data/usage-history/_set-aside/{aside}, but rewriting it without the line failed ({error}): the line is still in the file. VibeSpace reads past it and tries again the next time it reads the file.

What: line {line} of data/usage-history/_held/{file} is no record VibeSpace writes. VibeSpace kept every other record of the file and removed the line — data/usage-history/_set-aside already holds {over} files, so no copy of it was kept.

What: line {line} of data/usage-history/_held/{file} is no record VibeSpace writes. VibeSpace kept every other record of the file and set the line aside: the file as it was, bytes intact, is data/usage-history/_set-aside/{aside}.

What: line {line} of data/usage-history/_held/{file} is no record VibeSpace writes. VibeSpace read every other record of the file and read past the line; it could not set the file aside ({error}) and tries again the next time it reads it.

What: line {line} of data/usage-history/_held/{file} is no record VibeSpace writes. VibeSpace read past the line and kept the file as it is: data/usage-history/_set-aside already holds {over} files, so no copy was kept, and changing the file failed ({error}). It tries again the next time it reads the file.

What: line {line} of data/usage-history/_held/{file} — the record of an older hold of {month} — is no record VibeSpace writes. VibeSpace read the file's other records (their count is said for {month}), then moved the file as it was, bytes intact, to data/usage-history/_set-aside/{aside}.

What: line {line} of data/usage-history/_held/{file} — the record of an older hold of {month} — is no record VibeSpace writes. VibeSpace read the file's other records (their count is said for {month}), then removed the file, as it removes every older record once it is read; data/usage-history/_set-aside already holds {over} files, so no copy was kept.
What: while data/usage-history/{shard} was out of shape, the events of {month} were held beside it (at most {bound}); the rest of them are in the ledger now.

When a background job finishes, fails, is parked, or needs input, its owner conversation gets a message through Claude Code’s own cross-session messaging inbox (delivered by the CLI under its inbound rules; an idle session starts a turn, billed like a typed prompt).
